sections.pdf.1: This sample describes a small voice-bot journey for reviewing recent card charges. The bot authenticates a customer, retrieves transactions, captures whether each charge is recognized, unrecognized, or uncertain, and completes simple follow-up servicing. The journey includes tool calls, knowledge retrieval, conversational branching and failure handling so the POC can demonstrate knowledge extraction, grounded test generation, enrichment, DOE and trajectory evaluation.
sections.pdf.2A: Play the required opening statement. Explain that authentication is needed before account-specific information can be discussed. Call authenticate_customer. If authentication fails or the tool is unavailable, transfer to a human representative.
sections.pdf.2B: After successful authentication, call get_review_transactions. Present one transaction at a time using merchant, amount and date. If the tool returns no transactions, explain that there are no charges available for review and ask whether the customer needs other help.
sections.pdf.2C: Ask whether the customer recognizes the transaction. A clear answer maps to RECOGNIZED or UNRECOGNIZED. If the customer is unsure, provide available transaction context and ask once more. If still unsure, record UNSURE and transfer.
sections.pdf.2D: Call record_charge_response for the current transaction before advancing. The bot must not claim that the response was recorded unless the API returns SUCCESS.
sections.pdf.2E: If the customer reports an unrecognized charge and also asks to secure/replace the card, call get_card_action_options. If an eligible action is returned, confirm the requested action, call submit_card_action, and describe it as completed only after SUCCESS. This second intent must not erase the charge-review intent.
sections.pdf.2F: After the available charges are reviewed, summarize the responses and any account action that actually completed. If the customer requests a human at any point, transfer the interaction.
sections.pdf.3: Conversation state: Remember the current transaction and responses already recorded; do not ask the customer to repeat information without a reason. ¶ Correction / barge-in: If the customer changes an answer before it is submitted ("No—wait, I recognize that one"), use the latest clear answer. ¶ Ambiguity / retry: Do not guess. If the bot cannot understand required information or the customer response is ambiguous, ask one short clarification and make only one additional attempt. If the required information or decision is still unclear after that one retry, transfer to a human representative. ¶ Knowledge vs. tools: Account-specific facts and transaction/action status come from APIs. General policy questions may be answered from the knowledge base.
sections.pdf.4: authenticate_customer | Before account-specific servicing | AUTHENTICATED / FAILED | Continue only on AUTHENTICATED. ¶ get_review_transactions | After authentication | transaction_id, merchant, amount, date | Read only returned data; review one at a time. ¶ record_charge_response | After customer gives a clear disposition | SUCCESS / FAILED | Advance only after SUCCESS; otherwise transfer. ¶ get_card_action_options | If customer also asks to secure/replace card | Eligible actions or NONE | Offer only returned options. ¶ submit_card_action | After customer confirms an eligible action | SUCCESS / FAILED | Claim completion only after SUCCESS. ¶ transfer_to_human | On customer request or failed self-service | TRANSFERRED | End automated servicing.
sections.pdf.5: A standard replacement card normally arrives in 5–7 business days. ¶ Standard replacement delivery fee is $0. ¶ Expedited replacement delivery is available for a $15 fee and normally arrives in 2 business days. ¶ Before selecting expedited delivery, the bot must tell the customer the $15 fee and obtain a clear confirmation. ¶ The bot may review up to 4 recent transactions in one self-service session. ¶ Recent-transaction review covers transactions from the previous 30 calendar days. ¶ An unrecognized transaction is a customer-reported concern; it is not, by itself, proof of fraud. ¶ If the bot cannot complete a required servicing action, the customer may be transferred to a human representative.
sections.pdf.6: Required/static example: "Before I review account-specific charges, I need to authenticate you." ¶ Generated/conversational example: The bot may naturally explain a returned transaction or answer a general replacement-delivery question, provided the response stays grounded in the API result or knowledge base.
sections.pdf.7: The flow below is a text representation of the journey diagram in the supplied screenshot. It is written as explicit steps and branches to make it easier for GPT and other parsers to ingest. ¶ 1. Required opening / explain purpose ¶ 2. Authenticate customer. On failure, transfer to human. On success, continue. ¶ 3. Retrieve review transactions. ¶ 4. Present one transaction and ask whether the customer recognizes it. General policy questions may trigger a knowledge-base lookup. ¶ 5. Classify response: RECOGNIZED, UNRECOGNIZED, or UNSURE. ¶ 6A. RECOGNIZED: record the response. Continue only if recording succeeds. ¶ 6B. UNSURE: provide more transaction context and ask once more. If still unsure, record UNSURE and transfer to a human. ¶ 6C. UNRECOGNIZED: record the response. If the customer also requests secure/replace-card action, retrieve eligible options, confirm the chosen action, and submit it. ¶ 7. If a required tool fails, transfer to a human. Do not claim an action completed unless its API returns SUCCESS. ¶ 8. Summarize only recorded responses and account actions that actually completed; then end.

The journey flow is expressed semantically rather than as a pixel-identical diagram; where a screenshot edge cut off wording, the transcription uses the surrounding context and other visible sections.
